agent_notes: בְּנֵי אֵלִים is rendered 'sons of gods' (divine beings), not KJV 'O ye mighty'. The commentaries split: Metzudat David has angels, Ibn Ezra the stars, Rashi and Meiri the rulers/patriarchs' descendants (Israel). The plain sense, with Ps 89:7 and the Ugaritic bn ilm, is the heavenly court. The Targum's 'company of angels' supports it.
The Hebrew verse includes the superscription 'A psalm of David' as words 1-2 (the KJV numbers it as verse 0).

מַבּוּל occurs only here and in Genesis 6-11 (the Flood). I keep 'the Flood' and not a general 'deluge', so the allusion to Noah stays; the commentaries (Ibn Ezra, Radak, Targum) read it so. The verb 'sat' is read both as enthroned over the Flood and as 'sat as king at the Flood'; I keep the ambiguity with 'to the Flood he sat'.

history.note: [consider] Describe the present 'sits' as a reading of the wayyiqtol (as KJV, YLT and ASV take it), not as a tense the Hebrew marks; drop 'proper noun' for mabbûl. (PS.29.10: 'יָשָׁב' HVqp3ms 'he sat'; 'וַיֵּשֶׁב' Hc/Vqw3ms 'and he sat'; YLT 'hath sat … sitteth'.)

agent_notes: STEPBible glosses עַל as 'is over'; I render 'upon/over'. The 'many waters' are the cosmic waters of the heavens and the sea, as the Mekhilta/Radak tradition and a Baal-style storm theophany suggest. This is my reading; the commentaries disagree (rain, the Sea of Reeds, nations).

history.note: [consider] Mark the Ugaritic/Baal comparison as modern comparative scholarship, distinct from the cited commentators. (PS.29.3 commentaries: Radak reads the sea (מי הים), Ibn Ezra rain, Rashi the Sea of Reeds; none mention Canaanite myth.)
[consider] Say 'to the strength of Israel' rather than 'of each hearer'. (PS.29.4 Rashi: 'צִמְצֵם אֶת קוֹלוֹ לְפִי כֹּחָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל'.)

agent_notes: Addressed the reviewer request: the Piel point on וַיְשַׁבֵּר is now my own grammatical observation, supported only by the Targum's paired verbs (מַתְבַּר / וְתַבַּר); no BDB citation.
The five English versions agree except YLT, which takes שֹׁבֵר as a participle ('is shivering') — I keep the participial force in the literal layer.

agent_notes: Addressed the reviewer request: the aurochs/rīmu and Septuagint remarks are my own philological observations with no lexicon cited; Ibn Ezra and Metzudat Zion are cited only for what the packet quotes. 'Sirion' is the Sidonian name of Hermon (Deut 3:9), which the registry also reflects (loc.hermon_mount); that identification is my own knowledge, not from the packet commentaries, which say only 'names of mountains'.
Subject of וַיַּרְקִידֵם is the LORD (continuing v.5, the voice in v.5 is His); the suffix -ם refers back to the cedars. Rashi reads cedars and mountains together at Sinai; I keep the plain sense.

agent_notes: Kadesh: the packet links the name to loc.kadesh (the Negev oasis), but a northern Kadesh on the Orontes has been proposed because the storm runs north (Lebanon, Sirion) to south. I mention both in the commentary and do not decide. Rashi equates it with Sinai.

אַיָּלוֹת: 'does' (so Targum, Ibn Ezra, Rashi's first reading), but the Radak passage cites a view (Lowth's) that it means terebinths (אֵלוֹת), which parallels 'forests'. I follow the animal reading and flag the alternative in the notes. וַיֶּחֱשֹׂף is vocalised as an imperfect with waw (not a perfect), which I render in the present.
«Бней элим» переведено «сыны богов» в буквальном слое, как в английском; Синодальный перевод читает «сыны Божии». В драматическом слое выбрано «сыны богов» с пояснением «небесный совет».
Синодальный текст процитирован точно; сказано только то, что в нём верно: прошедшее «восседал» и будущее «будет восседать» для второго глагола.
